keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 1806 the Bourbon state is the island. Cliopatria draws Sicily inside the Napoleonic row for 1806-1814; the mainland is kingdom-of-naples-napoleonic. Murat's 'attempt to annex Sicily' failed (page, undated).

ledger.note: 1735: Charles of Bourbon becomes King of Naples and Sicily. 'Both Naples and Sicily were conquered by a Spanish army during the War of the Polish Succession in 1734'; he 'was installed as King of Naples and Sicily from 1735'; the Peace of Vienna of 18 November 1738 finalised it (Presidi page). The extent is Cliopatria's 1762 shape bridged back.

May 1735: the Presidi pass to the Bourbons. 'a Spanish and allied army conquered the Presidi in May 1735, and a preliminary peace in October 1735 confirmed the conquests'; the Emperor 'issued a diploma ceding the Presidi to him' on 11 December 1736; the Treaty of Turin of 1733 had agreed that 'Don Carlos should receive the Presidi together with the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily'. Porto Longone on Elba had never been Austrian, so only the Orbetello district is gained.

region.text: the Presidi: Porto Ercole, Orbetello, Talamone, Monte Argentario and Porto Santo Stefano

ledger.note: 23 December 1798: Ferdinand flees Naples for Palermo. 'on 23 December 1798, Ferdinand fled Naples to Palermo as a French army closed in.' The Parthenopean Republic page: he 'embarked on Nelson's Vanguard and fled with his court to Palermo'.

21-23 January 1799: the Parthenopean Republic is proclaimed. 'On 21 or 23 January 1799, the Parthenopean Republic was proclaimed' after French troops under Duhesme took Pescara in December 1798; it 'divided the former kingdom's territory into departments'. The mainland goes; Sicily stays with the king.

13 June 1799: the Republic ends. 'The republic existed from 21 January to 13 June 1799'; 'On 13 June 1799. Ruffo and his troops reached Naples'; 'The last Jacobin stronghold, Pescara, surrendered on June 30.'

10 July 1799: Ferdinand returns to Naples. 'On 10 July 1799, King Ferdinand entered the Bay of Naples.' Reviewer fix 2026-10-25 (eu-13-j review): confidence lowered from 3 to 2, because the page has the king entering the Bay of Naples on a frigate, not the court moving back to Naples; when the court left Palermo is not on the page.

28 March 1801: the Treaty of Florence takes the Presidi. 'By the Treaty of Florence of 28 March 1801, the king of Naples ceded the Presidi to the French Republic', with his rights on Elba (Porto Longone); France 'ceded them to the new Kingdom of Etruria', formally on 19 September 1801; 'Piombino and Elba, however, remained under the French.'

region.text: the State of the Presidi and his rights on Elba (Porto Longone)

ledger.note: 1806: the court moves to Palermo. 'Ferdinand IV and Maria Carolina fled to Sicily, and Palermo became their new capital.' The page gives no month.

February 1806: the French take the mainland. 'Capua was taken by the French on 6 February'; 'On 15 February, Joseph Bonaparte solemnly entered the city of Naples'; Napoleon proclaimed him King on 30 March 1806. Gaeta held out for almost five months and 'British troops defended Calabria and even scored a victory at Maida on 4 July'.

1814: the island monarchy is the same state that returns to Naples in 1815. 'Ferdinand IV was restored to the throne of Naples'; the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies was established on 8 December 1816. The dossier ends at Cliopatria's last year for this row; the Two Sicilies row starts in 1815.

region.text: Sicily, where Ferdinand had retained his throne

wars.name: War of the Polish Succession (conquest of Naples and Sicily)
wars.outcome: 'Both Naples and Sicily were conquered by a Spanish army ... in 1734'; the Presidi in May 1735; preliminary peace October 1735; definitive Peace of Vienna, 18 November 1738.
wars.note: Dates for the Presidi and the Peace of Vienna are from the Presidi page; the Kingdom of Naples page gives only 1734 and 1735.

wars.name: French invasion of Naples and the Parthenopean Republic

zones.text: the mainland of the former kingdom

wars.outcome: French troops took Pescara in December 1798; Ferdinand fled to Palermo on 23 December; the Republic was proclaimed on 21 or 23 January 1799 and fell on 13 June to Ruffo's counter-revolution; Pescara surrendered on 30 June; Ferdinand returned on 10 July.
wars.note: The infobox also gives 'French invasion: 21 January 1799', which conflicts with the December 1798 text.

wars.name: French conquest of the Kingdom of Naples (1806)
wars.outcome: Capua fell on 6 February and Naples on 15 February 1806; Gaeta fell after almost five months; the British won at Maida on 4 July; Ferdinand kept Sicily.
wars.note: Infobox 'Battle of Campo Tenese: 10 March 1806' (Kingdom of Naples page).

certainty.note: The realm's frontier with the Papal States is the old Neapolitan one (no treaty line is on the pages opened); the Presidi were fixed by the Peace of Vienna (18 November 1738) and the Treaty of Florence (28 March 1801). Sicily and the mainland are sea-bounded.

notes:
New state written by this batch: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic)' row (1762-1814) is two states, and its Bourbon-era shapes (1762, 1799, 1800, 1803) have no other home. The dossier lists the same Cliopatria Name as kingdom-of-naples-napoleonic and reviews only the shapes of 1762-1805; the Napoleonic shapes (1806, 1811, 1814) are reviewed there with Sicily taken out and placed here as a new 1806 keyframe. Slug from slugify('Kingdom of Naples (Bourbon)'). Wikipedia and Wikidata are those of 'Kingdom of Naples' (Q173065, the id Cliopatria gives its 1285-1501 row); the other group's kingdom-of-naples dossier may overlap the 1501-1734 span (Spanish and Austrian rule) through the eu-13-x additions.
The Bourbon realm continues as the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies; ending the dossier in 1814 is Cliopatria's row boundary, not a collapse. Sicily's 1806-1815 status (British-protected, the constitution of 1812) is not on any page opened.
Page budget: 5 pages for this and the Napoleonic dossier together (Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic), Neapolitan War, Parthenopean Republic, Kingdom of Naples, State of the Presidi); the Wikipedia pages Treaty of Florence (1801) does not exist (url_not_found). Unverified: the 1762 extent before 1762, whether the Presidi cells of Cliopatria's 1762 shape cover Porto Longone, the 1759 date of Ferdinand's accession (the page says 1759 for Charles's inheritance; the 1759 date for the reign is the page's wording).
